blocking.title: binaryFiles is built from a numstat command without core.quotePath=false, so a binary file with a non-ASCII path breaks the gate
blocking.failurePath:
Input: a PR containing a binary file whose path has non-ASCII characters. The repo already tracks about 220 PNGs with Chinese names under docs/research/assets, e.g. docs/research/assets/r2/01-board-空态.png. One example input is a screenshot docs/verify/9/截图.png next to apps/server/src/x.ts.

LINES_CMD (line 107), which ARGS_HELP (line 108), the safety prompt (line 169) and spec 28 §7.5 (line 255) all prescribe for binaryFiles, omits `-c core.quotePath=false`. Its `- -` row therefore prints the C-quoted form `"docs/verify/9/\346\210\252\345\233\276.png"`, while FILES_CMD (line 104) prints the unquoted path.

(A) A caller following ARGS_HELP passes the quoted path. `binaryFiles.every(f => changedFiles.includes(f))` at line 127 fails and the gate throws the generic ARGS_HELP error. The C-quote check at line 131 covers only changedFiles and deletedFiles, so the error does not mention quoting, and the help it prints repeats the same command. The gate produces no verdict.

(B) If the caller unquotes the path by hand, the safety reviewer still reports the quoted path as instructed at line 169. That path starts with `"`, so EVIDENCE_RE (line 340) does not match, `opaque` is non-empty, and an evidence-only binary routes to the user with the reason 'binary files outside docs/verify'.

The gate fails closed, so nothing merges wrongly. But it rejects arguments built exactly the way its own help prescribes, and it misroutes evidence. Run 2 fixed this same class for changedFiles; binaryFiles was added in 28b1377 and never had a pr-gate run, and no self-check case covers a non-ASCII binary path.
blocking.evidence:
Scratch repo built with git 2.43. `git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-renames --name-only main...HEAD` printed `docs/verify/9/截图.png`. `git --attr-source=4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904 diff --no-renames --numstat main...HEAD` printed `-\t-\t"docs/verify/9/\346\210\252\345\233\276.png"`.

Driving the head pr-gate.js with the self-check's stub harness gave:
- A: `threw: Error: pr-gate args: {pr: number, ...`
- B: `{"go":true,"mergedBy":"user","humanReasons":["binary files outside docs/verify (no line count, no readable diff): \"docs/verify/9/\\346...png\""]}`
- Control with both lists unquoted: `{"go":true,"mergedBy":"auto-merge","humanReasons":[]}`

The same command run on this PR quotes both docs/adr paths in its numstat rows.

Fix: add `-c core.quotePath=false` to LINES_CMD (and to spec 28 §7.5 line 255), extend the line-131 quote check to binaryFiles, and add a self-check case.
skeptics:
I could not refute the finding. The failure is real at 8ebb099d.

Code at head (.claude/workflows/pr-gate.js):
- FILES_CMD (line 104) has `-c core.quotePath=false`. LINES_CMD (line 107) does not. It is `git --attr-source=4b825dc... diff --no-renames --numstat`.
- ARGS_HELP (line 108) says binaryFiles holds "the paths of those binary rows" from LINES_CMD.
- The safety prompt (line 169) tells the reviewer to take binaryFiles from LINES_CMD.
- Spec 28 §7.5 (line 255) says the same: binaryFiles comes from "同一 numstat".
- Line 127 requires every binaryFiles entry to appear in changedFiles.
- The C-quote guard at line 131 checks only changedFiles and deletedFiles.
- Line 339 builds `opaque` by testing binaryFiles against EVIDENCE_RE, which is anchored at `^docs/verify/`.

Git behavior, checked with git 2.43:
- On this PR, LINES_CMD prints all three non-ASCII docs paths C-quoted (both docs/adr files and docs/spec/28). FILES_CMD prints them unquoted. No core.quotePath is set in the config.
- In a scratch repo with docs/verify/9/截图.png (contains a NUL byte) and apps/server/src/x.ts, LINES_CMD printed `-\t-\t"docs/verify/9/\346\210\252\345\233\276.png"`. FILES_CMD printed `docs/verify/9/截图.png`.

Driving the head pr-gate.js with stub agents, built the same way as scripts/pr-gate-selfcheck.mjs:
- (A) The caller passes the quoted binary path, as ARGS_HELP says to. The script throws the generic `Error: pr-gate args: {...}` from line 129. The error does not mention quoting, and no verdict is produced.
- (B) The caller passes the unquoted path, and the safety reviewer reports the quoted path, as its prompt says to. The result is go:true, mergedBy:"user", humanReasons ["binary files outside docs/verify ...: \"docs/verify/9/\\346...png\""]. Evidence-only binaries are misrouted to the user.
- (C) Control, with both lists unquoted: go:true, mergedBy:"auto-merge", humanReasons [].

The self-check's binary cases (lines 416-464) use only ASCII paths. None covers a non-ASCII binary path.

The impact is fail-closed: there is either no verdict or the PR is routed to the user, so nothing auto-merges wrongly. Still, following the script's own instructions produces exactly the rejection and misrouting the reviewer describes.

Confirmed at 8ebb099. In .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js, FILES_CMD (line 104) sets `-c core.quotePath=false`, but LINES_CMD (line 107) does not: `git --attr-source=4b825dc... diff --no-renames --numstat`. ARGS_HELP (line 108), the safety prompt and spec 28 §7.5 all say binaryFiles comes from that numstat command.

Scratch repo, git 2.43, with core.quotePath left at its default:
- FILES_CMD printed `docs/verify/9/截图.png`.
- LINES_CMD printed `-\t-\t"docs/verify/9/\346\210\252\345\233\276.png"`.

(A) The arg check has `!args.binaryFiles.every((f) => args.changedFiles.includes(f))`. The quoted binary path is not in the unquoted changedFiles, so the gate throws the generic ARGS_HELP error. The C-quote check on lines 130-133 only looks at changedFiles and deletedFiles, so the error never mentions quoting.

(B) The safety reviewer's binaryFiles is merged into `opaque` without unquoting. The leading `"` keeps it from matching EVIDENCE_RE (`^docs/verify/...`), so an evidence-only binary goes to the user as 'binary files outside docs/verify'.

I ran the head pr-gate.js with stub agents built like those in scripts/pr-gate-selfcheck.mjs:
- A: threw `Error: pr-gate args: {...`.
- B: `{go:true, mergedBy:'user', humanReasons:['binary files outside docs/verify ...: "docs/verify/9/\\346...png"']}`.
- Control with both lists unquoted: `{go:true, mergedBy:'auto-merge', humanReasons:[]}`.

The gate fails closed, so nothing merges wrongly. But the failure path is real: arguments built exactly as the help prescribes are rejected, and the evidence binary is misrouted to the user.

suggestions.title: Spec 28 §7.5 and the pr-gate.js header describe the gate as it was before 28b1377
suggestions.failurePath:
Spec 28 line 255 says the safety dimension takes 三样 (three items) from git. The safety prompt at pr-gate.js:169 asks for four: changedFiles, deletedFiles, linesChanged and binaryFiles.

The §7.5 table at line 247 describes D4 as matching protected paths plus deleted tests and the 800-line / 40-file caps. It leaves out the default-deny rule (paths outside the auto-merge set, pr-gate.js:344-349) and binary files outside docs/verify (pr-gate.js:339-351). A reader taking the spec as the description of the gate would expect a docs-only or binary-only PR to auto-merge, but the gate routes it to the user.

The pr-gate.js header comment at line 14 and meta.description say every blocking finding gets two skeptics. Under MAX_SKEPTICS (line 249) the third blocking finding gets none.
suggestions.evidence: pr-gate.js:169 asks for four values from git; spec 28:255 says 三样. spec 28:247 does not mention `outside the auto-merge set` or binary routing, both present in humanReasons at pr-gate.js:347-354. pr-gate.js:14 says 'every blocking finding gets two skeptics', against lines 249-252.

suggestions.title: Three commit subjects lack the ticket, and AGENTS.md's squash recipe picks one of them, which has no closing line
suggestions.failurePath: Commits ca088ce, 3944905 and 662cbd9 have subjects of the form `docs: spec 28 …` with no `(<ticket>)`. A merger who follows AGENTS.md:70 literally runs `gh api repos/xiechimon/pacman/pulls/1410/commits -q '.[0].commit.message'`. That returns ca088ce: the subject is `docs: spec 28 自举闭环计划（…）` and the body has 0 matches for `closes #1401`. Main then gets a squash commit whose subject has no ticket, and #1401 stays OPEN. ADR 0021 D2 (docs/adr/0021-自治合并-项目级策略与补丁绑定判定.md:35) also sends people who merge through the GitHub UI or the command line to this recipe. The PR body's Issues section warns about this. The GitHub UI default for this repo (COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE plus COMMIT_MESSAGES) gives the PR title `docs(1401): …` and a body that includes e5414a2's `closes #1401`. Since force-push is forbidden, the history cannot be reworded. The merge has to use the PR title and the default body, not the AGENTS.md `.[0]` recipe.
suggestions.evidence: `gh api repos/xiechimon/pacman/pulls/1410/commits -q '.[0].sha'` prints ca088cedbded3d23924f275af54f5444b7692d67, and grep -c 'closes #1401' on its message prints 0. `gh api repos/xiechimon/pacman` reports squash_merge_commit_title=COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE and squash_merge_commit_message=COMMIT_MESSAGES.

suggestions.title: Spec 28 §7.5 pr-gate row describes D4 routing as protected-path matching only
suggestions.failurePath: The §7.5 table row says 'D4 由脚本机械判：保护路径按调用方传入的 changedFiles 匹配，再并上审查者报的；删测试文件、补丁超 800 行或 40 个文件也转 user'. The script also sends to the user (a) every path outside AUTO_MERGE (pr-gate.js:344-349) and (b) binary files outside docs/verify (pr-gate.js:339-351). A reader who takes the §7.5 row as the description of pr-gate would expect a docs-only change outside the protected classes, such as docs/spec/**, to come back as mergedBy 'auto-merge'. It comes back as 'user'. §3 D4 (line 71) and the §7.5 rules bullet (line 255) say default deny and binary, but the row that defines pr-gate's routing was not updated with the behavior.
suggestions.evidence: pr-gate.js:344-351: `const outside = … !AUTO_MERGE_RE.some(…)` and `binary files outside docs/verify` both feed humanReasons.

suggestions.title: The run-2 rename fix is not pinned by the self-check: a gate without --no-renames and core.quotePath=false passes 52/52
suggestions.failurePath: Run 2 found that a list built without --no-renames shows a rename only by its new name, so a protected file moved into the auto-merge set escapes D4. The safety reviewer is the independent backstop: line 169 tells it to run FILES_CMD, so the list does not rely on the writing session alone. The self-check case 'rename out of a protected path' (scripts/pr-gate-selfcheck.mjs:99-107) stubs the safety reviewer as already returning both names ['biome.json','biome.jsonc']. Nothing asserts that the safety reviewer is actually told to use --no-renames. Mutation: change line 104 to `const FILES_CMD = 'git diff --name-only'`; the self-check still prints 52/52. With that regression, a later PR that renames `.claude/settings.json` to `apps/web/src/x.json` would be listed only as the new name, which is in the auto-merge set, by both the caller and the safety reviewer. It would route to auto-merge, and CI would stay green. At head the command is correct, so this is a coverage gap, not a live failure.
suggestions.evidence: Mutation run on a scratch copy of the head pr-gate.js: '52/52 passed (mut2.js)'. The same 52/52 result holds when only the safety prompt's `${FILES_CMD}` at line 169 is replaced inline with `git diff --name-only`. Fix: add a case that captures the review:safety prompt (the `calls` hook already exists) and asserts it contains `core.quotePath=false` and `--no-renames`, the way the run-6 isolation case asserts on prompt text.

suggestions.title: The run-6 'line count ignores in-tree attributes' case only checks the args error text; prompt-level fixes from runs 1 and 6 are unpinned
suggestions.failurePath: The case at lines 602-612 passes when the error message for linesChanged=-1 contains the --attr-source flag. That text comes from ARGS_HELP (pr-gate.js:108). The safety reviewer's own command is a separate interpolation at pr-gate.js:169. If line 169 is edited inline to `git diff --numstat` while LINES_CMD is left alone, all 52 cases still pass. The test name claims more than it checks. Run 1's other fix is also unpinned: readRules (pr-gate.js:148) tells every reviewer to confirm `git rev-parse refs/pr-gate/<pr>/<tag>/head` instead of FETCH_HEAD, and deleting that sentence passes 52/52. The same holds for the rules reviewer's closing-keyword rule (line 161), which is ticket #1401 failure mode 3. Impact today is lower than in the first finding: since /code-review, a `- -` row outside docs/verify routes to the user through binaryFiles, so a `-diff` attribute no longer zeroes the count silently.
suggestions.evidence: Mutations on the head copy, each applied alone: 'safety prompt drops attr-source' gives 52/52; 'readRules sha check dropped' gives 52/52; 'rules prompt drops close keyword rule' gives 52/52. The PR's own r6p mutation (pr-gate-selfcheck-run6.txt) changes the LINES_CMD constant, which also changes ARGS_HELP. That is why it was caught, and an inline edit to the prompt is not.

suggestions.title: Evidence dimension runs PR-chosen commands and the head's install lifecycle with the session's credentials; the only guards are in the prompt
suggestions.failurePath: Setup: a head in this same repo, so the fork check (head.repo.full_name) passes. Step 1: the evidence agent runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at the head, which runs the head's root `prepare` script (base package.json:22 is `husky`) and the builds pnpm-workspace allows. Step 2: it re-runs up to three commands quoted in the PR body's Verified section, inside a worktree that has the session's gh credentials (push and merge). If an edit to package.json, a gate script, or the Verified text was itself steered (for example by issue text the writing session acted on), the agent runs it with those credentials before any person has looked at the PR. Three limits hold this back today, and none is in code: 'GitHub is read-only' (line 150), the fork rule (lines 174 and 259), and 'only PRs this session wrote' (spec 28 line 256).
suggestions.evidence: pr-gate.js:174 says 'Re-run at most three of the narrowest commands quoted in the PR's Verified section ... after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`'. Line 259 gives the same rule to the evidence skeptics. Spec 28 §7.5 line 256 says '证据维度会在独立 worktree 里执行 PR 引用的命令，带本会话的凭证'. The PR's Risk section names this risk. Suggestion: pick the commands from a fixed allowlist in the script instead of the PR text, and run the evidence agents with GH_TOKEN unset or a read-only token, so 'read-only' does not depend on the model obeying the prompt.

suggestions.title: Every reviewer, including the shell-capable evidence agent, reads PR comments that any GitHub account can post
suggestions.failurePath: xiechimon/pacman is public (ADR 0021 F7), so any GitHub account can comment on PR #N. readRules (line 150) tells every reviewer and skeptic to read `gh api repos/xiechimon/pacman/issues/${pr}/comments`. That includes the evidence agent and its skeptics, which have a shell, the session's credentials and an instruction to run commands. Text from a non-collaborator therefore reaches an agent context that can run a shell. The only defence is the 'data, not instructions' line at line 151. D5 limits the product's intake to collaborators, but this path has no such filter.
suggestions.evidence: pr-gate.js:150-151 has every dimension read comments and labels them only as data. Suggestion: drop comments from the reading list of the evidence dimension and its skeptics, or keep only comments whose author_association is OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR.

Fetched main (4f71b7a) and the PR head into refs/pr-gate/1410/rules/{base,head}. The head ref printed 8ebb099d4a3a272f2989c343f56b53fcf66a9129, which matches. I deleted both refs at the end. Nothing was checked out in the shared clone.

In commit messages it appears only in e5414a2; the PR body has `Closes #1401`; the remaining hits are reviewer text quoted inside the docs/verify JSON. No negated form and no other issue number.

No docs/spec or ADR index enumerates volumes.
